title: The World Keeps Its Smallest Secrets

sections.heading: Baseline
sections.text:
Before, the world was legible.
Tides kept their appointments. Cloud
came in eighths, as forecast.
Stars stood where the almanac
had left them.

I had a pencil for every coastline
and a unit for every sort of quiet,
down to the hush of a classroom
one second before somebody is asked a question.

A beach was a grid reference.
A sunset was a daily event,
timed to the minute, then forgotten.
Everything held still for the pencil.
Nothing I measured
ever argued back.

sections.heading: Arrival
sections.text:
There was no front. I want that noted.
No pressure drop, no bruise of cloud
along the western edge.

You came in mid-sentence,
halfway through a story
that had clearly started without me
and was, by the sound of it, going well.

The needle on the barometer moved
the width of a hair, then pretended
it hadn’t. I logged it as a draught.

And somewhere between one bell
and the next, an ordinary corridor
acquired coordinates.

sections.heading: Small Things
sections.text:
The evidence was always small enough
to lose in a pocket:

the second question, the one that proves
you heard the answer to the first;

an aside somebody made once,
on the way to saying something else,
handed back to them a week later
with interest;

your voice changing key between two words,
a joke crossing into something true
without stopping at the border;

the way you go still when someone talks,
the way a compass goes still,
settling not on the thing they said
but on the thing they said it for;

a quiet person at the edge of a table,
drawn back into the conversation
by a question only they could answer;

the corner of your mouth
giving a laugh away
three seconds before you allow it;

and the aliens, who like
whatever you like, and whom you quote
with a completely straight face:
an advanced civilisation
with remarkably local taste.

sections.heading: Measurements
sections.text:
So I took readings.

I weighed a bad day before
a single joke, and after,
and the difference was small
and would not stay small.

I timed a sentence you said in passing,
one you have since forgotten.
It is still running. So is the stopwatch.

I paced the beach in metres. It came out
the same as always, and also
as an evening.

I logged the arguments and followed
each one upstream, looking for the source,
and found a dry bed
and two people
defending the river anyway.

Reading 31 was voided,
owing to a pig.

sections.heading: Instrument Failure
sections.text:
Then the instruments
began to disagree with themselves.

The barometer read *fair*
through a week of rain.
The clock in the corner lost eleven minutes
to a conversation
and would not say where.

I divided one laugh by one corridor.
The answer would not terminate.
It recurs. It is recurring now.

The ~~solar incidence~~ late light
across your face, halfway
through an argument,
went into the log as instrument error,
there being no column wide enough.

I sent the whole file for audit,
flagging every entry
where the numbers started lying.
It came back stamped:
all of them true.

sections.heading: The Legend
sections.text:
The fault, when I found it, was in the aim:
I had pointed every instrument at you,
and every one had turned, quietly,
to read the room you had just walked through.

Nothing moved. I want that
on the record too.
The sand weighed what sand weighs.
The sun went down as printed
over a sea that kept its own counsel.

You never touched the map.
What changed was the legend,
that small box in the corner
nobody reads, which tells you
what the symbols mean.

A line that meant *shore*
now means a particular evening.
A dot that meant *corridor* means
something was said there.
A blank that meant *afternoon*
has a name I keep
not writing down.

And you, out on a court before
the light has made up its mind,
turning a dark morning into a plan,
look at the horizon the way
a navigator looks at blank paper:
not as an edge. As the part
nobody has drawn yet. The horizon,
I gather, has been informed.

Twice now I have watched
somebody standing next to you
reach for a pencil.

sections.heading: After
sections.text:
The world keeps its smallest secrets
where anyone could find them:
in a corridor, in the second question,
in a sentence nobody meant
to be remembered, kept anyway.

I have stopped trying to prove it.
Erratum, throughout:
for *measure*, read *notice*.
I leave the instruments running
and the window open,
and write down the weather.

Tonight: wind light. Tide on time.
Stars where the almanac left them, roughly.
Cloud, four eighths. One argument
about nothing, unresolved,
both parties satisfied.
Needle: still a hair off true.

Visibility, for no reason
any instrument can find,
further than before.
